device.model: ROSMASTER M3 Pro with the DOFBOT-Pro arm
device.name: Yahboom ROSMASTER M3 Pro

facts.text: The M3 Pro is a mecanum chassis carrying the DOFBOT-Pro arm; its motors sit behind an STM32 expansion board running micro-ROS firmware, reached through ROS 2 Humble and micro_ros_agent
The base is /cmd_vel (geometry_msgs/Twist): linear.x forward, linear.y strafe, angular.z yaw, SI units
The firmware zeroes the motors after roughly 200-500 ms without a fresh Twist, so a held move is a stream at the publish rate followed by an explicit zero
The arm is /arm6_joints (arm_msgs/ArmJoints): all six servos at once as joint1..joint6 in integer degrees plus time in milliseconds
Joints 1-4 travel 0-180 degrees, joint 5 travels 0-270, and joint 6 is the gripper from 30 (closed) to 180 (open)
The board holds a commanded arm pose, so one /arm6_joints message is enough
The servo travel table is 1-4: 0-180, 5: 0-270, 6: 30-180 degrees, the vendor limits every Yahboom teleop node clamps to
The model joint q maps to servo degrees as deg = 90 + degrees(q), so +-pi/2 maps onto 0-180 for joints 1-4 and -pi/2..pi onto 0-270 for joint 5
The gripper crank rlink1 travels -1.54 (closed) to 0 (open), mapped linearly onto 30-180 degrees
The vendor keyboard-teleop ceilings are a linear speed limit of 1.0 m/s and an angular speed limit of 5.0 rad/s
The longest one move may hold a twist is MAX_MOVE_DURATION_S = 10.0 s; a longer run is repeated calls
The board publishes no arm joint-state topic this driver can verify: get_observation returns {} on the robot rather than echoing the last command as a reading
The arm holds its pose on its own; only the base can be moving
stop_task sends a zero Twist, and it is not exempt from the /cmd_vel operator gate: the halt needs a pre-approved /cmd_vel or an approving operator
set_arm_degrees refuses an angle outside each servo's travel rather than clamping it
